SYNTHETIC LAB & DESIGN
Sovereign Federation Lab / Reader guide · edition 09

Keep business services. Add governed federation.

Reuse existing banking services. A loosely coupled sovereignty layer governs location and movement; business services retain the interactions.

Proposed pilot design

This page describes a target design. The local lab and browser models demonstrate bounded subsets; the proposal is not production acceptance. Understand the labels.

Start with the example · Look up a term

Two responsibilities, working together

Start with the services already running in the bank. A contact service still updates contact information; a holdings service still applies its product rules. The sovereignty layer supplies placement and authority decisions and manages approved copies. The receiving business service uses a permitted view; a copy never becomes a second master.

ResponsibilityBusiness servicesSovereignty services
PurposeOwn banking interactions, business rules and operational records.Govern approved data location, write authority and policy-scoped copies.
Facts and decisionsSupply ownership, relationship context, consent and classification facts.Combine trusted facts with grants, exclusions and placement; OPA evaluates the applicable rules.
ChangeValidate a command and commit its business effect, mandatory audit and export intent locally.Deliver approved copies asynchronously; track receipts, restrictions and live-copy cleanup.
AccessServe the approved business view and enforce the caller’s permitted action and purpose.Supply current placement and authority checks; guard imports and projection reads.

Deploy peers alongside participating services

Proposed pilot design. Deploy the same sovereignty component in each approved region that participates in sharing. Configure its entity/store bindings, local policy and narrow service credentials. Each peer connects to existing business services through adapters and to other peers through private authenticated export/import endpoints. A peer may support several services or entities; sharing a deployment never merges their permissions.

01Existing business service

Keeps its API, interactions and authoritative banking records.

02Local sovereignty peer

Resolves approved placement and governs export, import and current authority.

03Approved recipient peer

Accepts a permitted projection for the recipient business service.

The normalized lab schema illustrates these contracts. Map existing business keys and relationships through an adapter; adopting the example tables or consolidating all business services is not a prerequisite. The lab does not yet supply a generic peer installer or integrations for an existing bank estate.

Integrate only where the service participates

ParticipationRequired integration
No governed shared dataNo federation adapter is needed. Existing authentication, local controls and any applicable residency obligations still apply.
Read a shared viewUse an authorised query adapter that checks recipient, purpose, current policy and approved location before returning the projection.
Create or change shared dataReuse a compatible transactional outbox or add a local transaction hook for resource bindings, versions, export intent and mandatory audit. Cover every writer of that governed data.
Bulk loads, direct SQL or maintenanceUse the same governed mutation contract or restrict write credentials. Unregistered changes must not silently bypass the controls.

Loose coupling does not mean zero integration. Local business commit and remote delivery are separate. The local hook shares the existing transaction; it does not call a remote sovereignty service while that transaction is open. An existing event stream is reusable only if it preserves the required atomic intent, ownership, scope and version information. A raw changefeed alone does not establish that contract.

Business APIs and workflows remain with their services. The adapter boundary contains placement lookup, local mutation intent, guarded query and approved import/export. See the detailed integration contract.

Read and write routing answer different questions

The gateway or service adapter selects a route using trusted ownership and a versioned placement directory supplied by the sovereignty layer. Business services execute the interaction. A route does not grant access. Check caller, recipient, purpose, fields and processing location as well as storage location; moving a request body through a prohibited region is already a prohibited crossing.

RequestWhere it goesWhat must hold
Write a relationship or holdingThe current authoritative owner’s business service.Business validation, current writer authority and a permitted processing path. A recipient projection is not writable as the owner.
Read an approved local viewThe recipient’s business service over its local projection.Current permission and placement, approved fields, and freshness acceptable to that business interaction. A stored copy alone is insufficient.
Read requiring the latest committed business stateThe owner service, only when that processing path is permitted.Authorisation and an explicit freshness requirement. If a lawful fresh read is unavailable, report unavailable or pending; do not widen access.
Write after an entity migrationThe new owner location after fenced cutover.Refresh the verified placement and authority version. The old writer rejects stale requests even if a router cached the old address.

No nearest-store fallback, automatic writer promotion or unrestricted cross-region read fan-out is implied. Unknown authority or missing mandatory policy fails closed for the affected operation. A replica or telemetry outage need not undo a valid owner commit; required authority checks and transactional audit remain mandatory.

Follow one Singapore contact update

01Route the command

An authorised UK interaction resolves the Singapore owner and uses an explicitly permitted processing path.

02Commit at the owner

The Singapore business service applies its rules and commits contact, versions, export intent and audit together.

03Move the approved view

The source peer enforces exclusions before export; UK rechecks and commits only the allowed copy. US receives no excluded relationship data.

04Read with an explicit need

A UK service can use its permitted local view when freshness allows. A read requiring the latest state uses a lawful owner path or reports pending/unavailable.

Minimal party identity has its own eligibility and grants. Its presence in the US does not permit a US relationship read or write.

What the lab proves, and what the pilot must add

The real container lab proves local SQL business/outbox/audit commits, OPA-scoped projections and guarded recipient reads. Those reads check current policy and placement but can return an older ordinary data version. They consult owner authority; there is no offline authority lease or automatic owner-read fallback.

The isolated India migration proves source fencing and stale-write rejection for its separate fixture. Migration of normalized business tables, independent peer deployment, authenticated routing, an API freshness contract and distributed authority remain pilot work. Read the proposed integration and routing decision or inspect this guide’s executed checks.

Technical reference: local transactions and API contracts

Deployment and access

ComponentPoC nowRegional target
GatewayLoopback FastAPI endpoint; no authenticationRegional Envoy/Kong or equivalent + identity + local OPA admission + rate/size limits.
Business modulesParty, Contact/Consent, Relationship, Holdings, History in one processExisting regional services with bounded sovereignty adapters; share a local UoW only where invariants require it, otherwise preserve explicit service consistency contracts.
Owner routerTrusted synthetic entity directory in harnessResolve owner and physical home from authenticated context; reject or lawfully forward wrong-home request.
Policy/export workerLocal OPA + polling outboxLocal OPA; CDC outbox intents → regional Kafka → egress gate.
Recipient query/importSingle harness uses typed regional tablesIndependent credentialed importer and query service; OPA admission, scopes and receipts.
ObservabilityOTel command, gate and import spansRegional collectors, approved aggregates, governed audit archive.
No global body-terminating gateway by default

Regional gateways authenticate the caller and validate legal entity, service action and purpose. Forwarding customer payloads is itself governed processing. An independent global party service can expose only its approved minimum and must not reveal unauthorised relationship existence. The PoC deliberately does not implement these production authentication controls.

Follow one contact update

Business success is returned after the owner transaction commits. The destination is eventually consistent. Reconciliation uses current authoritative facts and can coalesce earlier intents; it does not promise to deliver every intermediate business version.

Concrete transaction boundaries

OperationOne local transactionAsynchronous follow-up
Update contactContact + selected preference + history + both affected scope versions + outbox + audit + request receiptRe-evaluate personal and business graphs independently; party minimum unchanged.
Open holdingHolding + owner-only alternate ID + classification + bindings/rules + scope version + intentExport whitelisted holding fields; no balance or core identifier.
Withdraw consentRelationship-specific consent + history + decision revision + intentRead blocked against stale authorisation receipt; remove contact/preference projection.
Table/key restrictionParallel control facts + affected epochs + intents + audit receiptAll affected scopes re-evaluated; global default cannot override denial.
Recipient replaceDelete child-first; insert parent-first; manifest + inbox + auditSource acknowledgement recorded after destination commit.

API outline

EndpointContract
GET /api/operationalSource graph, controls, typed destination rows, queue and receipts; owner-only diagnostic scope in production.
POST /api/operational/scopes/{id}/commandsrequest_id UUID, expected_version, command and synthetic fields; 409 stale version or conflicting replay.
GET /api/operational/scopes/{id}/preview/{entity}Current actual OPA row decisions + dependency closure; read-only.
GET /api/operational/scopes/{id}/read/{entity}Current purpose/entitlement/placement and decision epoch; then recipient graph.
POST /api/stores/{id}/pausePoC fault injection for delayed import; not a production business endpoint.

Performance choices with explicit trade-offs

The thin implementation replaces complete small graphs, polls every 800 ms and processes up to 15 operational deliveries per pass. It uses a single process lock, model scans and one source writer to make races reviewable. This is not a throughput design or benchmark. Production should use indexed binding lookups, bounded manifests, per-scope/destination partitions, local connection pooling, backpressure and retry budgets.

Very high party fanout should update a durable resource epoch and mark dependent scopes dirty in bounded batches. Reads must check the current resource authorisation epoch so delayed fanout cannot extend revoked access. Ordinary contact-value freshness may lag; consent/geography narrowing must fail closed. Keep WAN and policy transport outside local transactions and add serialization retry with idempotency.

Keep the transactional outbox as the business boundary. A future CockroachDB changefeed can publish outbox intents to regional Kafka. Changefeeds are at-least-once and do not preserve transaction-wide ordering; use a current connected manifest and an inbox rather than replaying unrelated table events as though they were atomic.

Walkthrough and engineering gates

01Global versus scoped

US sees Aster party minimum, no relationship. Example Trading party excluded.

02Shared update

Change contact once; two relationship versions advance.

03Revoke during pause

Pause London, withdraw consent, observe stored copy and denied read; resume removes rows.

04Narrow by table or key

Owner-only contact table; party US exclusion; restricted holding.

05Verify real adapters

Run SQL, OPA, crash/replay tests and inspect regional OTel. No inferred residency guarantee.

Validation and sources

Executed: 840 operational browser/OPA cases (7,290 row decisions), Python graph/command tests, Node workflow tests and original 12 Rego / 990 entity parity checks. The subsequent unified Docker suite passed actual SQL commands/projections, API restart persistence and trace-correlated OTLP logs in Loki. The live Chromium walkthrough passed. The source supplies executable acceptance and typed SQL checks; database crash boundaries, accessibility, regional isolation and pilot load remain separate gates.

For implementers: engineering brief
HAND OFF TO ENGINEERING

Build this component

A focused prompt with scope, contracts and acceptance criteria.

Read the full prompt
Extend existing banking services through bounded adapters; preserve their business APIs and ownership. Treat independent sovereignty peers and authenticated routing as pilot work. Integrate writers of governed shared data with a compatible atomic outbox or local hook, durable audit and current versions. Enforce source exclusions, guarded recipient reads, permitted processing paths, explicit freshness and fenced owner writes. Do not require estate-wide service consolidation, a new banking master or remote calls inside the owner transaction. Preserve and run the real CockroachDB/OPA lab acceptance gates.
